findings.summary: Imports use literal .ts extensions ('../../db/client.ts', './schema.ts'); under NodeNext+verbatimModuleSyntax tsc -b emits TS5097 (allowImportingTsExtensions disabled). Same anti-pattern flagged blocking in wave-5 F-001.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 4 to `from '../../db/client.js'` and line 5 to `from './schema.js'` — match the .js-extension convention used by shared/logger.ts and modules/auth/tokens.ts. Confirm with `pnpm --filter @medbridge/api typecheck`.

findings.summary: All four src/ imports use literal .ts extensions (db/client.ts, modules/auth/passwords.ts, modules/auth/schema.ts, shared/logger.ts); each emits TS5097 and keeps `pnpm typecheck` red.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite lines 1–4 with .js extensions: `from '../db/client.js'`, `from '../modules/auth/passwords.js'`, `from '../modules/auth/schema.js'`, `from '../shared/logger.js'`. Re-run typecheck to confirm zero TS5097 in seed/.

findings.summary: insertRefreshToken's `rows[0]` triggers TS7053: `.returning()` infers `any[] | QueryResult<never>` because refreshToken's self-FK on `replacedBy` (wave-5 F-002, still open) leaks `any` into the schema. Adds a NEW tsc error this wave.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix upstream first (wave-5 F-002: annotate refreshToken's type or split the self-FK). Workaround here: cast `const rows = (await db.insert(refreshToken)...) as RefreshToken[]` or destructure with explicit type. Track jointly with F-002 of wave-5.

findings.summary: Imports the eager `db` singleton from db/client.ts; perpetuates the wave-3/4/5 eager-load anti-pattern and prevents buildApp(env)-style DI in wave-7/9 (auth service/routes will be locked to the module-load-time pool).
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor repo functions to accept a `Db` argument (or export a factory `createAuthRepo(db: Db)` returning the function set). Compose at buildApp() time once env + pool are constructed. Same posture as wave-5 F-003 and wave-4 F-002.

findings.summary: API drifts from task spec: task description says `notContainsAny(lines, [secrets...])` (two-arg helper). Implementation hardcodes `lines` to the capture's own buffer, so callers cannot assert against an externally supplied line array.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) change signature to `notContainsAny(lines: readonly string[], needles: readonly string[])` and have it close over neither, or (b) update the task spec / PRD to match the bound-method form. Option (a) keeps the helper composable.

findings.summary: test/support files import src/ modules with literal .ts extensions (db/client.ts, db/schema.ts). test/ is excluded from tsconfig.include so tsc is silent now, but inconsistent with project's .js-extension convention and will break if tests are later added to typecheck.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite '../../src/db/client.ts' → '../../src/db/client.js' (and similarly for schema.ts in db.ts/fixtures.ts and the other test/support files). Aligns with src/ convention.

findings.summary: SEED_PLAINTEXT literal duplicates the SEED_PASSWORD default in apps/api/src/seed/main.ts; if either string changes without the other, integration tests pass against a non-canonical credential.
findings.suggested_fix: Either source both from a single constant exported from the seed module, or add a CI assertion that the two values match. Task description explicitly chose duplication; noting for retro.

findings.summary: insertSeedUsers uses emails `patient@seed.test` / `doctor@seed.test`, distinct from seed/main.ts's `patient@medbridge.test` / `doctor@medbridge.test`. Intentional fixture/seed separation but worth recording so future cross-tests don't assume identical identities.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the deliberate divergence in apps/api/test/support/fixtures.ts header comment (or in test-layout.md when intel-refresh runs) so future authors don't accidentally unify them.
